q: A payee reports that a cheque issued by the Railways in his favour has been lost before encashment. The correct course is to:

options.A: Treat the original payment as cancelled and charge the amount afresh to working expenses
options.B: Issue a fresh cheque immediately, without any enquiry, and let both cheques remain live
options.C: Stop payment of the lost cheque, ascertain from the bank that it has not been paid, and then issue a fresh cheque in lieu of it
options.D: Ask the payee to wait till the close of the financial year, when a fresh cheque will automatically be issued

q: A cheque issued by the Railways has become time-barred without being encashed, and the payee now surrenders it and asks for payment. Payment is made by:

options.A: Extending the date on the old cheque itself with a correction slip
options.B: Writing back the amount of the old cheque in the books and issuing a fresh cheque in lieu of it
options.C: Paying the amount in cash from the imprest of the Accounts Officer without any entry
options.D: Debiting the amount to Traffic Suspense and paying it from station earnings

q: A cheque issued by the Railways is cancelled at the instance of the drawing office before it is paid by the bank. In the books, the cancellation is given effect to by:

options.A: Crediting the amount to Sundry Other Earnings
options.B: Making no entry, as the cheque was never paid
options.C: Debiting the amount to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: Debiting the head 'Cheques and Bills' and crediting back the head of account originally debited when the cheque was issued

q: Wages and salaries drawn for disbursement to staff, but remaining undisbursed at the close of the month, are accounted for by crediting the amount to:

options.A: The head 'Unpaid Wages', held under the debt/deposit heads pending disbursement or claim
options.B: Sundry Other Earnings of the Railways
options.C: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: Cash-in-Transit

q: Amounts held under the head 'Unpaid Wages' are subsequently paid to the staff entitled to them. Such payments are accounted for by:

options.A: Charging them afresh to the working expenses of the month of payment
options.B: Crediting them to 'Demands Recoverable'
options.C: Debiting them to the Pension Fund
options.D: Debiting them to the head 'Unpaid Wages', thereby clearing the amount held under that head

q: Wages held under the head 'Unpaid Wages' which remain unclaimed beyond the prescribed period are:

options.A: Retained under the head permanently
options.B: Transferred to the Railway Safety Fund
options.C: Forfeited to the paying officer's office as miscellaneous cash
options.D: Treated as lapsed and credited to the revenue of the Railways, in the same manner as other lapsed deposits

q: Labour welfare works, such as staff welfare amenities other than passenger amenities, are financed from the subdivision of the Development Fund known as:

options.A: DF-I
options.B: The Railway Safety Fund
options.C: DF-III
options.D: DF-II

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Works of road safety at level crossings, financed from the Railway Safety Fund, are classified under Plan Head 29.
2. Works of road safety relating to road over-bridges and road under-bridges, financed from the Railway Safety Fund, are classified under Plan Head 30.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The third and last batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants during a financial year is ordinarily presented to Parliament in the:

options.A: Monsoon Session
options.B: Winter Session
options.C: Budget Session
options.D: A special session convened after the close of the year

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Budget Estimates from the Revised Estimates?

options.A: The Budget Estimates are the estimates for the ensuing year which are presented to and voted by Parliament, whereas the Revised Estimates are a re-estimate of the current year's receipts and expenditure, prepared during the year and not voted by Parliament
options.B: The Budget Estimates relate only to capital expenditure, whereas the Revised Estimates relate only to revenue expenditure
options.C: The Revised Estimates are voted by Parliament, whereas the Budget Estimates are not
options.D: The Budget Estimates are prepared in January, whereas the Revised Estimates are prepared in February

q: In the accounts of the Government of India, the Consolidated Fund of India forms:

options.A: Part I of the Government accounts
options.B: Part II of the Government accounts
options.C: Part III of the Government accounts
options.D: A part of the Public Account of India

q: Under Article 280 of the Constitution, besides recommending the distribution of taxes, the Finance Commission is also required to recommend measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of:

options.A: The Zilla Parishads only
options.B: The Railway Board
options.C: The Panchayats and Municipalities in the State
options.D: The State Public Service Commission

q:
Consider the following statements about a Financial Bill of the second category, that is, a Bill which, if enacted, would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India but does not contain any of the matters specified in Article 110(1):
1. Such a Bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
2. Such a Bill cannot be passed by either House unless the President has recommended its consideration by that House.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: After the Appropriation Bill is passed by the Lok Sabha and transmitted to the Rajya Sabha, the Rajya Sabha:

options.A: Can amend the Bill and insist on its amendments
options.B: Can only return the Bill with its recommendations, if any, the procedure being the same as for a Money Bill
options.C: Must pass the Bill within six months
options.D: Has no role at all, the Bill going directly to the President from the Lok Sabha

q: An amount debited to the suspense head 'Demands Recoverable' for services rendered by the Railways to an outside party is cleared from that head when:

options.A: The party renders services of equal value to the Railways
options.B: The close of the financial year is reached, whether or not the amount is realised
options.C: The amount is written off by the Traffic Accounts Office
options.D: The amount is actually realised from the party and the head is credited with the realisation

q: An amount credited to the head 'Demands Payable' for goods and services received by the Railways is cleared from that head when:

options.A: Payment is actually made to the party concerned and the head is debited with the payment
options.B: The goods are returned to the supplier in every case
options.C: The next year's budget is voted
options.D: The amount is transferred to the Capital Fund

q: When a railway asset is sold, dismantled or otherwise finally disposed of, its original cost is:

options.A: Retained in the Block Account permanently, even after disposal
options.B: Transferred to the Pension Fund
options.C: Removed from the Block Account, so that the Block continues to represent only the assets in existence
options.D: Written off against the earnings of the year in which the asset was created

q: The sale proceeds realised on the disposal of a capital asset of the Railways, such as surplus land or a building, are accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting them to Sundry Other Earnings as a revenue receipt
options.B: Crediting them to the capital head concerned, as a reduction of the capital outlay on the Railways
options.C: Crediting them to the Development Fund in all cases
options.D: Holding them under Traffic Suspense till the next budget

q: In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, the External Debt of the Central Government is classified under Major Head:
Which of the following correctly distinguishes the classification of the working expenditure of Commercial Lines from that of Strategic Lines?

options.A: The working expenditure of Commercial Lines is classified under Major Head 3002, whereas that of Strategic Lines is classified under Major Head 3003
options.B: Both are classified under Major Head 5002
options.C: The working expenditure of Commercial Lines is classified under Major Head 3003, whereas that of Strategic Lines is classified under Major Head 3002
options.D: Both are classified under Major Head 3001

q: A work of track renewal is financed from the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh. In the classification of accounts, the work continues to be classified under:

options.A: A separate Plan Head created for the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh
options.B: Plan Head 31, Track Renewals, the source of finance being indicated as RRSK in the allocation
options.C: Plan Head 21, Rolling Stock
options.D: Sub-Major Head 12 of Major Head 3002

q: Stores are supplied by the stores depot of one zonal railway to another zonal railway for use on the receiving railway. The cost of the stores is adjusted between the two railways:

options.A: By the receiving railway remitting cash daily to the supplying railway
options.B: Through the Contingency Fund of India
options.C: By debiting the amount to the earnings of the supplying railway
options.D: Through transfer transactions, the supplying railway raising a debit against the receiving railway

q: The apportionment of earnings from parcels traffic carried over more than one railway is dealt with in the Traffic Book in:

options.A: Part A, parcels being a part of Coaching earnings
options.B: Part B, along with goods earnings
options.C: Neither part, parcels earnings being never apportioned
options.D: A separate Part C maintained for parcels traffic

q: Scrap stores are sold by the Railways for an amount which differs from their book value in the stores accounts. The difference between the sale value and the book value is adjusted through:

options.A: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.B: Sundry Other Earnings
options.C: The Stock Adjustment Account
options.D: Traffic Suspense

q: The Stock Adjustment Account in the stores accounts is operated to adjust:

options.A: Only the differences in the quantities of stores found on verification
options.B: Only the interest on stores balances
options.C: Both price (value) differences and quantity differences in stores
options.D: The differences between the earnings budget and the actual earnings

q: During the physical verification of stores in a depot, a shortage of stores is found against the book balance, and the shortage is not explained by the stockholder. The value of the shortage is adjusted in the accounts through:

options.A: The Stock Adjustment Account, pending recovery or write-off with competent sanction
options.B: The earnings of the depot for the month
options.C: The Pension Fund
options.D: The Works Register of the division

q: The security deposit of a contractor, held by the Railways under the 'Deposits' head, becomes refundable on the satisfactory completion of the work. The refund is accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting the 'Deposits' head afresh
options.B: Debiting the 'Deposits' head, thereby clearing the liability held under it
options.C: Charging the amount to ordinary working expenses
options.D: Crediting the amount to the Capital Fund

q: The earnest money deposited by the successful tenderer with his tender is ordinarily:

options.A: Forfeited to the Railways in every case
options.B: Refunded in cash on the day the tender is opened
options.C: Credited to Sundry Other Earnings
options.D: Retained and adjusted towards the security deposit payable by him under the contract

q: The cut motions which can be moved in the Lok Sabha during the discussion and voting of the Demands for Grants are of:

options.A: Two types — policy cut and token cut
options.B: One type only — the token cut
options.C: Four types — policy cut, economy cut, token cut and guillotine
options.D: Three types — policy cut, economy cut and token cut

q: In the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways, the sanctioned provision against which the actual expenditure on 'charged' items is compared is termed the:

options.A: Final Grant
options.B: Final Appropriation
options.C: Budget Allotment
options.D: Revised Estimate

q: The March (Preliminary) Account Current rendered by a zonal railway serves mainly to:

options.A: Enable the Railway Board to close the accounts of the year in time, on the basis of the figures then available, the March (Final) Account Current following with the remaining adjustments
options.B: Present the Budget Estimates of the following year
options.C: Report only the balances under the suspense heads for March
options.D: Obtain the Vote on Account for the following year

q: Ways and Means Advances made by the Reserve Bank of India to the Government of India are:

options.A: Interest-free grants made out of the Public Account
options.B: Advances on which interest is charged by the Reserve Bank, being in the nature of a temporary loan
options.C: Contributions made by the Reserve Bank to the Railway funds
options.D: Advances which are never required to be repaid

q: The pay and allowances of the staff actually engaged on the construction of a new railway line are charged in the accounts to:

options.A: The ordinary working expenses under Major Head 3002 in all cases
options.B: The Pension Fund
options.C: Sundry Other Earnings
options.D: The capital cost of the work concerned, as part of the outlay on the work

q: The renewal of a bridge is financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund. The work is classified under the allocation:

options.C: Capital-3200

q: Receipts from cloak rooms and left-luggage offices at railway stations are classified in the railway accounts under:

options.A: Passenger earnings
options.B: Goods earnings
options.C: Other Coaching Earnings
options.D: Sundry Other Earnings

q: Items held under the suspense heads of account are normally cleared by:

options.A: Adjustment (transfer) entries crediting or debiting the final heads of account to which the items properly belong
options.B: Cash payments made by the Cash & Pay Office in all cases
options.C: Writing them off at the end of every month without sanction
options.D: Transferring them to the Railway Board's earnings

q: The Committee on Public Undertakings of Parliament examines, among others, the reports and accounts of the railway public sector undertakings, such as IRCTC and IRFC, in order to satisfy itself that:

options.A: Their trains are running to time
options.B: Their affairs are being managed in accordance with sound business principles and prudent commercial practices
options.C: Their staff are paid the correct rates of pay
options.D: Their earnings are apportioned correctly among the zonal railways

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the monthly compilation of the accounts of a zonal railway?

options.A: Account Current — Trial Balance — Classified Abstract — Ledger
options.B: Ledger — Account Current — Journal — Trial Balance
options.C: Subsidiary Books — Classified Abstract — General Books (Ledger) — Trial Balance — Account Current
options.D: Trial Balance — Subsidiary Books — Account Current — Classified Abstract

q: The Internal Debt of the Central Government, classified under Major Head 6001, comprises broadly:

options.A: Only the loans raised by the Railways through IRFC
options.B: Market loans, treasury bills and other internal borrowings of the Government, including securities issued against small savings
options.C: Only the external loans raised from foreign governments
options.D: The balances held in the Public Account of India

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence of the stages through which the annual budget cycle of the Railways is completed?

options.A: Appropriation Accounts — Budget Estimates — Voting of Demands — Actual expenditure
options.B: Budget Estimates — Voting of Demands and Appropriation Act — Actual expenditure against the grant — Appropriation Accounts
options.C: Actual expenditure — Budget Estimates — Appropriation Accounts — Voting of Demands
options.D: Voting of Demands — Appropriation Accounts — Budget Estimates — Actual expenditure

q: Items of expenditure or receipts which are held under objection during internal check in the Accounts Office, pending regularisation, are entered and watched in a register known as the:

options.A: Register of Earnings
options.B: Objectionable Item Register
options.C: Works Register
options.D: Liability Register

q: An amount has been entered in the Objectionable Item Register because a payment was made in the Accounts Office's check without the required sanction. The item is cleared from the register when:

options.A: The close of the financial year is reached, whether or not the objection is settled
options.B: The item is transferred to another suspense head of account
options.C: The objection is settled by recovery of the amount, by regularisation under competent sanction, or by write-off where so sanctioned
options.D: The dealing assistant certifies that the item is old and may be dropped

q: The findings of the periodical inspection of a divisional or unit accounts office, or of the initial records of an executive office, carried out by the Accounts Department are communicated to the office concerned through:

options.A: A Transfer Certificate
options.B: The Debt Head Report
options.C: The monthly Account Current
options.D: An Inspection Report, the compliance with which is watched till the objections raised are settled

q:
Consider the following statements about inspection of accounts offices and records by the Accounts Department:
1. The objections raised in an inspection report are pursued with the office inspected till they are settled or regularised, and are not dropped merely with the passage of time.
2. Such inspection is a part of the statutory audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The internal check exercised over the earnings of the Railways is directed mainly to ensuring that:

options.A: The expenditure at stations does not exceed the budget allotment
options.B: The staff at stations are paid their salary on the due dates
options.C: All amounts due to the Railways by way of earnings are correctly demanded, realised and brought to account, so that no earnings are omitted or lost
options.D: The earnings are apportioned among the zonal railways every month

q:
Consider the following statements about the arrangement of payments in a zonal railway:
1. The Cash & Pay Office makes payment only against bills and payment orders which have been passed for payment by the Accounts Office.
2. This separation of the passing of bills in the Accounts Office from the actual disbursement by the Cash & Pay Office is itself an element of the system of internal check.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The balances shown in the subsidiary registers maintained in the Accounts Office, such as the Suspense Registers, are agreed periodically with:

options.A: The Station Balance Sheets rendered by the stations
options.B: The corresponding balances recorded in the General Books (Ledger) of the railway, any difference being investigated and set right
options.C: The figures of the Railway Board's Pink Book
options.D: The bank scrolls received from the accredited bank alone

q:
Consider the following statements about the cash held by cashiers and imprest holders on the Railways:
1. The cash balance held by a cashier is verified only by the cashier himself, and no other check is considered necessary.
2. The cash balances held by cashiers and other holders of cash are subject to verification by the Accounts Department through periodical and surprise checks.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: In the Accounts Office of a zonal railway, the maintenance of the General Books (the Ledger and the Journal) and the compilation of the monthly Account Current from them is the work of the:

options.A: Books (compilation) section of the Accounts Office
options.B: Cash & Pay Office
options.C: Traffic Accounts Office alone
options.D: Executive engineering office of the division

q: In the accounting system of the Railways, the 'link heads' serve the purpose of:

options.A: Linking the salary bills of staff with their Provident Fund accounts
options.B: Recording the transactions between a station and the Cash Office
options.C: Linking the suspense heads of one zonal railway with those of another
options.D: Connecting the detailed commercial classification of accounts maintained by the Railways with the Major Heads of the Government accounts, so that railway transactions are incorporated in the accounts of the Government of India

q:
Consider the following statements about the linkage between the railway accounts and the Government accounts:
1. The transactions of the Railways are taken into the accounts of the Government of India through the corresponding Government Major Heads, which function as link heads between the two systems of classification.
2. It is this linkage which enables the Railways to maintain their own detailed commercial classification while their results are exhibited in the Government accounts under the prescribed Major Heads.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Wagons owned by one zonal railway are worked for a period on another zonal railway. The hire charges due to the owning railway for the use of its wagons are settled by:

options.A: Transfer transactions between the two railways, the hire charges being credited to the owning railway through the inter-railway adjustment
options.B: Daily cash remittance by the using railway to the owning railway
options.C: Crediting the amount to Sundry Other Earnings of the Railway Board
options.D: Adjustment against the earnings originated by the using railway at its stations

q:
Consider the following statements about inter-railway adjustments:
1. Hire charges for rolling stock are a part of the traffic earnings and are divided among railways in Part A of the Traffic Book along with passenger earnings.
2. Hire charges payable for the use of another railway's rolling stock form part of the inter-railway financial adjustments and are settled through transfer transactions, without movement of cash.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A station is jointly served by two zonal railways and the staff and facilities at the station are common to both. The expenses of the joint station are:

options.A: Borne wholly by the railway on which the station building is situated, in all cases
options.B: Charged to the Contingency Fund of India
options.C: Recovered from the passengers using the station as a surcharge
options.D: Shared between the two railways on the basis prescribed or agreed between them, each railway's share being adjusted through transfer transactions

q: A road over-bridge is constructed in replacement of a level crossing under a cost-sharing arrangement between the Railways and the State Government. In the accounts:

options.A: The entire cost is charged to the Railways, the State Government's share being ignored
options.B: The entire cost is borne by the State Government as a deposit work
options.C: Each party bears its agreed share of the cost, the Railways accounting for their own share under the allocation of the work and recovering or adjusting the other party's share accordingly
options.D: The cost is held under Traffic Suspense till the bridge is opened to traffic

q: Under the Reserve Bank of India Act, the Reserve Bank is under an obligation to transact the banking business of the Central Government, that is to say:

options.A: It must accept money for and on account of the Central Government, make payments on its behalf and carry out its exchange, remittance and other banking operations
options.B: It must finance the fiscal deficit of the Central Government in full every year
options.C: It must audit the accounts of the Central Government before they are laid before Parliament
options.D: It must approve the Annual Financial Statement before its presentation

q: At centres where the Reserve Bank does not itself conduct the cash business of the Government, the receipts and payments of the Government are handled by:

options.A: The treasuries of the State Governments in all cases
options.B: The Cash & Pay Offices of the Railways
options.C: The Pay and Accounts Offices of the Ministries
options.D: Agency banks appointed by the Reserve Bank, which conduct Government business as its agents

q:
Consider the following statements about the Reserve Bank as banker to Governments:
1. The banking business of the Central Government is transacted by the Reserve Bank as a matter of agreement which either side may terminate at will without notice.
2. The banking business of the State Governments is transacted by the Reserve Bank under agreements entered into with the respective State Governments.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The core banking solution of the Reserve Bank of India, through which Government receipts and payments handled by the Reserve Bank are processed and accounted, is known as:

options.A: IPAS
options.B: e-Kuber
options.C: Bharatkosh
options.D: CIPS

q: The Public Financial Management System (PFMS) of the Government of India, implemented through the office of the Controller General of Accounts, is principally:

options.A: A system for the apportionment of railway earnings among zonal railways
options.B: A register of the suspense balances of the Government
options.C: The portal through which passengers reserve accommodation on the Railways
options.D: A central platform for payment, accounting and monitoring of the flow of Government funds, including releases under Government schemes

q: 'Bharatkosh', the Non-Tax Receipt Portal of the Government of India, provides:

options.A: A single-window facility for depositing the non-tax receipts of the Government of India electronically, the amounts being credited to the Government account
options.B: A portal for the payment of suppliers' bills by the Railways
options.C: A system for the electronic acceptance of inter-railway transfer transactions
options.D: A facility for passengers to claim refunds of fares online

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed by:

options.A: The Prime Minister of India
options.B: The Union Finance Minister
options.C: The President of India
options.D: A committee of both Houses of Parliament

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India can be removed from office:

options.A: Only in the like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court of India
options.B: By the President at pleasure, at any time
options.C: By a resolution of the Lok Sabha alone passed by a simple majority
options.D: By the Union Finance Minister with the approval of the Cabinet

q: After the Comptroller and Auditor General of India has ceased to hold office, he is:

options.A: Eligible for appointment as the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
options.B: Eligible for any office under the Government of India with the approval of Parliament
options.C: Required to join the Indian Audit and Accounts Service
options.D: Not eligible for further office either under the Government of India or under the Government of any State

q: The duties, powers and conditions of service of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India in relation to the audit of Government accounts are laid down in:

options.A: The General Financial Rules
options.B: The Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971
options.C: The Railway Finance Code, Volume I
options.D: The Government Accounting Rules

q: The statement relating to tax expenditure, presented with the Budget documents of the Government of India, shows:

options.A: The expenditure incurred by the Government on the collection of taxes
options.B: The arrears of taxes outstanding against the Railways
options.C: The estimated revenue forgone by the Government on account of the tax incentives, exemptions and concessions allowed under the tax laws
options.D: The share of taxes assigned to the State Governments

q: The Budget document titled 'Notes on Demands for Grants' primarily:

options.A: Records the votes cast by the members of the Lok Sabha on each Demand
options.B: Explains the nature, scope and reasons for the significant provisions made in the Demands for Grants
options.C: Contains the detailed classification of Major and Minor Heads of account
options.D: Lists the works included in the Railway Works Programme

q: The financial control exercised by the Public Accounts Committee over public expenditure is essentially:

options.A: Exercised before the expenditure is incurred, by way of prior approval of each Demand
options.B: Ex post facto in character, being exercised after the expenditure has been incurred, on the basis of the Appropriation Accounts and the audit reports thereon
options.C: Exercised only in respect of the charged expenditure of the Government
options.D: Exercised through the voting of the Demands for Grants in the Lok Sabha

q: In the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account of the Government, the Major Heads generally correspond to the functions of Government, while the Minor Heads below them generally correspond to:

options.A: The objects of expenditure
options.B: The departments which incur the expenditure
options.C: The funds from which the expenditure is financed
options.D: The programmes taken up under the function concerned

q:
Consider the following statements about the classification of Government accounts:
1. The List of Major and Minor Heads of Account is common to the Union and the State Governments, so that the accounts of the Centre and the States are maintained on a uniform classification.
2. Every State Government maintains its own entirely separate list of Major Heads, unrelated to the list followed by the Union Government.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: In the accounts of the Union Government, the share of the States in the net proceeds of the shareable Union taxes is exhibited:

options.A: As expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: As a voted Demand for Grant of the Ministry of Finance
options.C: As a deduction from the gross tax receipts of the Union, and not as an item of expenditure
options.D: As a disbursement out of the Public Account of India

q:
Consider the following statements about the statements laid before Parliament under the FRBM Act along with the Budget:
1. The FRBM statements are voted by Parliament along with the Demands for Grants.
2. The FRBM statements form a part of the Schedule to the Appropriation Act.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Long-outstanding items under the suspense heads of a railway are taken up for clearance by:

options.A: Writing them off at the close of every month without further enquiry
options.B: Transferring them to the Railway Pension Fund
options.C: Netting the debit items against the credit items under the head
options.D: Pursuing them with the units, offices or parties concerned, the oldest items being taken up on priority on the basis of an age-wise analysis of the outstanding items

q: The first line of budgetary control over expenditure on a railway rests with:

options.A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: The Public Accounts Committee of Parliament
options.C: The controlling and spending officers themselves, who are responsible for watching the progress of expenditure and the liabilities incurred against the allotments communicated to them
options.D: The accredited bank through which the payments are made

q:
Consider the following statements about the surrender of funds out of a grant:
1. Savings which are anticipated under a head should be surrendered as soon as they are foreseen, and should not be retained by the unit till the close of the financial year.
2. Funds once surrendered by a unit remain available to that unit for use on any other work of its choice.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The statutory audit of the accounts of a zonal railway is conducted locally on behalf of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India by:

options.A: The Principal Financial Adviser of the zonal railway
options.B: The Principal Director of Audit (Railway Audit) attached to the railway
options.C: The Controller General of Accounts
options.D: The internal audit party of the Railway Board

q: After the Public Accounts Committee has presented a report to Parliament, the action taken by the Government on the recommendations contained in the report is brought to the notice of the Committee through:

options.A: Action Taken Notes furnished by the Government, on which the Committee presents its Action Taken Report
options.B: A fresh Demand for Grant presented in the following Budget
options.C: The Appropriation Accounts of the following year alone
options.D: A resolution moved by the Finance Minister in the Lok Sabha

q: The qualifications for appointment as the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission are:

options.A: Prescribed in the Constitution itself, article by article
options.B: Decided by the President in each case without any law
options.C: Determined by Parliament by law, the governing enactment being the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951
options.D: Laid down in the General Financial Rules

q: Under the system of cash management of the Government of India, the Ministries and Departments are required to frame, for regulating their expenditure with reference to the ways and means position:

options.A: A Vote on Account for every quarter of the year
options.B: Monthly Expenditure Plans and Quarterly Expenditure Plans
options.C: A separate Contingency Fund for each quarter
options.D: Weekly statements of suspense balances

q: The monthly accounts of a State Government are compiled, under the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, by:

options.A: The Accountant General (Accounts and Entitlements) of the State concerned
options.B: The Controller General of Accounts, New Delhi
options.C: The Finance Secretary of the State Government
options.D: The Reserve Bank of India at Nagpur

q:
Consider the following statements about the watching of suspense balances:
1. Outstanding items under a suspense head are watched item-wise, with reference to the age of each item, and not merely as a single net balance under the head.
2. An item under a suspense head stands cleared only when it is traced to, and adjusted against, its final head of account or is recovered or paid, and not by merely netting it against an unrelated item.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The Governmental Accounting Standards Advisory Board (GASAB), set up in the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, is concerned with:

options.A: Fixing the rates of railway fares and freight
options.B: Auditing the accounts of the zonal railways
options.C: Preparing the Demands for Grants of the Ministries
options.D: Formulating and recommending accounting standards for the Government, for the Union and the States

q: A balance outstanding under 'PAO Suspense' in the books of a zonal railway, representing an amount paid on behalf of another Ministry, is finally settled:

options.A: Through the Reserve Bank by book adjustment, on the basis of the advice or confirmation of the Pay and Accounts Office concerned, and not by a cash payment between the offices
options.B: By the station staff of the railway out of the station earnings
options.C: By writing it off at the close of the financial year in every case
options.D: By debiting the amount to the working expenses of the zonal railway

q: The accounts of the railway public sector undertakings, being Government companies, are subject to audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, whose reports on them are:

options.A: Confined to the files of the Ministry of Railways
options.B: Laid before Parliament and examined by the Committee on Public Undertakings
options.C: Examined only by the Estimates Committee
options.D: Published only in the annual report of the Railway Board

q: The Budget Estimates of the Railways and the accounts actually compiled for the year are maintained under the same classification of heads of account. This identity of classification between the Budget and the accounts is necessary mainly so that:

options.A: The Pink Book can be printed in a single volume
options.B: The earnings of the Railways can be apportioned among the zonal railways
options.C: The actual expenditure of the year can be compared head-wise with the grants and appropriations sanctioned by Parliament, as is done in the Appropriation Accounts
options.D: The suspense balances can be carried forward to the next year

q: When an order of re-appropriation within a grant is given effect to in the budget allotments, the result is that:

options.A: The total amount of the grant sanctioned by Parliament is increased
options.B: The allotment under the receiving head is increased and the allotment under the donor head is reduced by the same amount, the total grant remaining unchanged
options.C: A fresh grant is created for the receiving head
options.D: The amount re-appropriated is transferred to the Public Account

q:
Consider the following statements about recording re-appropriation:
1. A re-appropriation is recorded against the heads concerned in the Budget Register, so that the allotment as modified, and not the original allotment alone, governs the watching of expenditure.
2. A re-appropriation order by itself creates an additional grant over and above the grant voted by Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A divisional officer finds an apparent saving under a head, but bills and commitments already incurred against that head, and recorded in the Liability Register, are still unpaid. Before surrendering any saving, the correct course is to:

options.A: Surrender the whole apparent saving at once, the unpaid bills being a charge on the next year's grant
options.B: Retain the whole provision till the close of the year without informing the headquarters
options.C: Provide for the liabilities already incurred and surrender only the net saving expected to remain after meeting them
options.D: Divert the apparent saving to a new work of his choice without sanction

q: During the course of the year, a unit foresees that a work provided for in its allotment will not be taken up and that the provision will remain unspent. The correct course for the unit is to:

options.A: Carry the provision forward for use in the following year on its own authority
options.B: Retain the provision and spend it in the closing months on any other item
options.C: Book the amount to a suspense head so that the grant does not lapse
options.D: Surrender the anticipated saving promptly to the controlling authority, so that the funds can be used elsewhere in the grant

q: The 'proportionate target' of earnings for a part of the financial year means:

options.A: The earnings actually realised in the corresponding period of the previous year
options.B: One-twelfth of the annual earnings budget for every month, in all cases
options.C: The total earnings budget of all the zonal railways taken together
options.D: The share of the annual earnings budget which, according to the budget proportions fixed for the year, is expected to be realised by the end of that period

q:
Consider the following statements about the evaluation of earnings against the Budget:
1. During the year, the actual earnings are evaluated against the proportionate earnings target for the period, and not merely against the annual Budget Estimates as a whole.
2. A shortfall of actual earnings against the proportionate target is examined, with reference to the trend of traffic, when the estimates are reviewed during the year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the compilation of the working expenditure budget of a zonal railway?

options.A: Railway Board — Ministry of Finance — divisions of the railway — zonal headquarters
options.B: Divisions and field units frame the estimates — zonal headquarters consolidates and scrutinises them — the Railway Board consolidates the estimates of all railways — the estimates are included in the Union Budget
options.C: Ministry of Finance frames the estimates — the Railway Board distributes them — stations incur the expenditure
options.D: Accounts Department frames the estimates alone — divisions approve them — Parliament votes them division-wise

q: The Revenue Budget of the Railways, as distinct from its Capital Budget, comprises:

options.A: The estimates of earnings and of working expenditure, including the appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund which form part of the working expenses
options.B: The annual plan outlay and the manner of its financing alone
options.C: The estimates of stores purchases alone
options.D: The balances under the debt and suspense heads alone

q: Which of the following correctly brings out the linkage between the Works Programme and the Capital Budget?

options.A: The Final Works Programme is drawn up first, and the Budget Estimates are framed afterwards from it alone
options.B: Proposals are submitted as the Preliminary Works Programme — the works approved are included in the Works Programme (Pink Book) with budget provision — after the grant is voted and the allotment communicated, the Final Works Programme for the year is drawn up
options.C: The works are sanctioned by Parliament through the Demands for Grants, and no Works Programme is prepared
options.D: The Capital Budget is prepared by the stores department from the Stores Budget alone

q:
Consider the following statements about works included in the Works Programme:
1. Inclusion of a work in the Pink Book does not by itself amount to sanction of the work.
2. For a work so included but not yet sanctioned, the budget makes only a token provision, a regular allotment following the sanction of the work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Under the performance-cum-outcome approach to budgeting, the progress of a work or scheme is judged primarily by:

options.A: The amount of the grant surrendered at the end of the year
options.B: The number of re-appropriation orders issued for the work
options.C: The speed with which the allotment is exhausted
options.D: The physical output and outcome actually achieved against the target, and not merely by the amount of money spent

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Outcome Budget from ordinary performance budgeting?

options.A: The Outcome Budget seeks to relate the financial outlays provided to the outcomes and deliverables expected from them, whereas performance budgeting frames the budget in terms of functions, programmes and activities together with the physical targets to be achieved
options.B: The Outcome Budget is a statement of suspense balances, whereas performance budgeting is a statement of earnings
options.C: Both are statements of the balances under the debt heads of account
options.D: The Outcome Budget is prepared by the Audit Department, whereas performance budgeting is prepared by the Cash & Pay Office

q: The amount authorised by the Appropriation Act for expenditure 'charged' on the Consolidated Fund of India is termed an 'Appropriation', as distinct from a 'Grant', because charged expenditure is:

options.A: Met out of the Public Account of India
options.B: Authorised by the Appropriation Act without being submitted to the vote of the Lok Sabha
options.C: Incurred only by the Railway Board
options.D: Not shown in the Demands for Grants at all

q:
Consider the following statements about the presentation of charged expenditure in the Demands for Grants:
1. The estimates of charged expenditure are presented in the Demands along with the voted estimates, but are shown separately from them.
2. Although charged expenditure is not voted, the amounts charged are nevertheless included in, and authorised by, the Appropriation Act.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A deposit work is in progress for an outside party and it becomes clear that the amount deposited by the party will not cover the cost of completing the work. The correct course is to:

options.A: Complete the work by charging the excess to the ordinary working expenses of the Railways
options.B: Watch the expenditure against the amount deposited and call upon the party to deposit the additional amount required, instead of charging the excess to the revenues or capital of the Railways
options.C: Stop accounting for the work altogether and drop the item from the books
options.D: Transfer the deposit to the earnings of the Railways and treat the work as a railway work
